roleContext.jobDescription: A beverage company runs three bottling plants. Its manufacturing execution system (MES) tracks batches, line stoppages and quality holds. The Software Engineer develops integrations between the MES, the plant PLC gateways and the ERP, maintains the line-stoppage dashboards, writes automated tests for the integration services, analyses recurring faults with the plant engineers and takes a place on the weekly out-of-hours support rota for the plants. The MES team has six engineers and reports to the head of manufacturing IT. Integration services are written in C#, run on servers at each plant and are released through Azure DevOps; the out-of-hours rota covers all three plants one week in five.

requirements.text: Develops integration services between the MES, plant PLC gateways and the ERP in C# or Java.
Builds and maintains production dashboards for line stoppages and quality holds.
Writes automated tests for integration services and runs them in the CI pipeline.
Works with plant engineers to analyse recurring line faults.
Takes part in the weekly out-of-hours support rota for the plants, responding to incidents remotely.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Software Engineer, Manufacturing Execution Systems

## Experience

- Developed C# integration services at Northmoor Dairies that link the MES to the OPC UA gateways on four filling lines and post completed batches to the SAP ERP.
- Built Grafana dashboards for line stoppages and quality holds, fed from the MES event tables and used at the plant's morning production meeting.
- Wrote xUnit integration tests with recorded gateway messages and ran them in the Azure DevOps pipeline on every merge.
- Handled daytime second-line support for the integration services, picking up tickets raised by the plant IT helpdesk.
- Met the plant engineers monthly to go through the top recurring line faults in the stoppage data and agree which ones needed a software fix.

## Work samples

- Work sample: a pull request adding retry and dead-letter handling to the batch-posting service, with the xUnit tests, the pipeline run log and the reviewer's approval.
